status_summary: Executive Order 14148 (signed 2025-01-20) revoked Executive Order 14094, Modernizing Regulatory Review (2023), and Executive Order 14192 (signed 2025-01-31) directed the OMB Director to revoke the November 2023 Circular A-4 and reinstate the 2003 version; OMB's circulars page lists only the 2003 version. EO 14192 also requires agencies to identify at least 10 existing regulations for repeal for each new one and lets the OMB Director set agency cost allowances. It does not name Executive Order 13771, but a Columbia Law School climate blog treats it as that order's successor. Executive Order 14294 (signed 2025-05-09) disfavors criminal enforcement of regulatory offenses, requires agencies to report their criminal regulatory offenses and to state mental-state standards in new rules; it covers the same subject as first-term Executive Order 13980, which the Mandate lists for revival, but does not name or reinstate it. The 2026 Unified Agenda introduction (2026-08-14) reports $211.8 billion in cost savings for fiscal 2025 and projects $1.5 trillion for fiscal 2026; these are administration figures. Congress passed Congressional Review Act disapproval resolutions in 2025 (a Wikipedia list counts 22 signed that year). This review found no enacted REINS Act or Midnight Rules Relief Act, no administrative pay-as-you-go requirement, no updated federalism or takings order, and no confirmed revival of Executive Order 13891 on guidance documents or the other first-term orders the Mandate lists.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 revokes Executive Order 14094 (Modernizing Regulatory Review, 2023), along with Executive Orders 13992, 13990 and 14008. It does not mention Circular A-4.

Executive Order 14192 (published 2025-02-06) requires agencies to identify at least 10 existing regulations for repeal for each new one, sets a fiscal 2025 total incremental cost for new regulations below zero, lets the OMB Director set later cost allowances, directs revocation of the 2023 Circular A-4 and reinstatement of the 2003 version, and reinstates the 2018 Treasury and OMB agreement on tax-regulation review.

Executive Order 14294, Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, is signed (published 2025-05-14, 90 FR 20363). It disfavors criminal enforcement of regulatory offenses, requires agencies to report their criminal regulatory offenses to OMB and post them, to state a mental-state standard in new rules with criminal consequences, and to publish guidance on referrals to the Justice Department. It covers the subject of first-term Executive Order 13980 but does not name or revoke any prior order.

Latest of the 2025 signings in a Wikipedia list of Congressional Review Act disapproval resolutions: 22 were signed in 2025, including three California vehicle waiver resolutions (2025-06-12), two CFPB rule resolutions (2025-05-09) and BLM plan resolutions (December 2025). The page lists no 2026 signings.

The 2026 Unified Agenda introduction describes Executive Order 14192's ten-for-one rule and agency designations as deregulatory, regulatory, exempt, waived or other, and reports $211.8 billion in cost savings for fiscal 2025 and a projected $1.5 trillion for fiscal 2026.
Date this review read OMB's circulars page, which lists only the 2003 version of Circular A-4 (dated 2003-09-17) and no 2023 version.
